clue.text: More voguish jail?

explanation.surface: A question about whether a prison could be more fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool means trendy, so cooler means trendier; separately, the cooler is informal slang for a prison cell.

clue.text: Award originally conveyed on horseback

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of the word conveyed

parts.note: a jockey riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: A trophy first carried in on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a trophy given to a winner, a type of award.

clue.text: Some cold, stern grandad, perhaps?

indicators.note: some means only part of the words cold stern is taken

explanation.surface: A grandfather who is a bit chilly and strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandad is an example of an elderly person, which is what the colloquial word means; hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dog compiler observed south of his glen, oddly

indicators.note: in this down clue the compiler is placed below the first part
oddly tells us the letters of his glen are arranged strangely

parts.note: a crossword's compiler is its setter

explanation.surface: A crossword maker's dog is spotted down in a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges HIS GLEN into ENGLISH; SETTER goes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The English setter is a gundog breed with a feathered speckled coat.

clue.text: Crazy general's assistant enthralled by chart

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the assistant is held within the chart

parts.note: a chart is a map
ADC, aide-de-camp, is an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: An unhinged military aide caught up in poring over a map.
explanation.walkthrough: ADC is the standard abbreviation for aide-de-camp, a senior officer's personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is wildly reckless, a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: A child Marryat abandoned in London landmark

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A foundling from a Captain Marryat novel left in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Marryat was a Victorian naval novelist. Admiralty Arch is the ceremonial gateway between Trafalgar Square and The Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty Arch is a famous Edwardian archway building in central London, a landmark.

clue.text: Flesh-eating mammal — one with fur, perhaps?

parts.note: a fur is a coat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A carnivore described as a single creature with a furry pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative of the Americas, classed as a carnivore.

clue.text: Favourite weapon to contain universal ill-humour

indicators.note: the weapon holds the letter within it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as teacher's pet
a lance is a weapon
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A beloved weapon holding a general bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky peevishness, a bad-tempered mood.

clue.text: Vagrant mongrel — quiet one with tail

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
I is the Roman numeral one
to tail someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A stray dog with a quiet nature and a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like a noun belonging to the dog, but it is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pi-dog (pye-dog) is an ownerless half-wild dog of Asian villages, a stray mongrel.

clue.text: Take steps with fellow politician to secure agreement

parts.note: CO, as in co-worker, means fellow or joint
MP, Member of Parliament
to take steps is to act

explanation.surface: Advice on working with a colleague in parliament to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a formal pact or contract between parties, an agreement.

clue.text: Manage to make ceremonial cloak

definitions.meaning: a long vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Instructions to sew a cloak for a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal with a situation; a cope is a priest's semicircular liturgical mantle.

clue.text: Dull piece of fabric we may wipe our feet on?

definitions.meaning: ..., also spelt matt, describes a surface without shine

definitions.text: piece of fabric we may wipe our feet on?

explanation.surface: A boring bit of cloth by the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat finish is lustreless, and a mat is the floor covering by a door for cleaning shoes.

clue.text: Operatic heroine caught leading man taking off

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a king is a leading man, a ruler

explanation.surface: A soprano grabs the star tenor as he departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' reads as departing but means imitating.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone off means impersonating them, which is copying or mimicking.

clue.text: Unbiased individual initially given role in distribution of mail

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word individual
in places the role inside the reshuffled letters
a distribution spreads things around, so the letters of mail are rearranged

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A neutral person gets a job sorting the post.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's postal sorting is the anagram: 'distribution of' scrambles the mail to MIAL, and 'in' sets the role after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial means not favouring either side, a synonym for unbiased.

clue.text: Like the Fens, ultimately rather quiet in May

indicators.note: in puts the following letters inside the month's name
ultimately picks the final letter of the word rather

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: The flat fenland is fairly peaceful in late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are a low-lying, formerly waterlogged region of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fens were wetland before drainage, so they are characteristically boggy, waterlogged ground.

clue.text: Uphill task, introducing a new motto

parts.note: a slog is hard, laborious work

explanation.surface: A hard struggle is relieved by a fresh catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase adopted as a watchword, a motto.

clue.text: Bird of prey old playwright's written in Greek

indicators.note: written in puts these letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the playwright

explanation.surface: A hawk from an ancient dramatist's Greek text.
explanation.definitionFit: The goshawk is a large hawk, a raptor that hunts other birds.

clue.text: Eyesore? What some animals live in, we're told

indicators.note: we are told it, so the word is heard spoken

parts.note: pigs live in a sty

explanation.surface: A pigpen is an ugly sight, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' literally: a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore of the eye.

clue.text: Vehicle access skirting front of posh woodwork

indicators.note: the two words go round either side of the letter, skirting it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
entry is a way in, access

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the word posh

explanation.surface: A driveway entrance edged with smart timber trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirting' looks like the woodwork of the surface (skirting board), but it signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the craft of working timber, and also the wooden parts it produces.

clue.text: Enthuse over northern bird

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first part above the next

parts.note: to rave is to enthuse wildly

explanation.surface: Getting excited about a bird from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Visit Bath and Wells for example

definitions.meaning: Bath and Wells is a diocese

explanation.surface: A suggestion to tour two Somerset towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath and Wells are cities in Somerset, England, jointly forming one diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area of authority, and to see a person is to call on them.

clue.text: Guest, popular girl, needing support on course

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet
a tee supports the ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: A sought-after young woman arrives at a golf club, propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitee is someone who has been invited, a guest.

clue.text: Prepared to study biology at last

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word biology

explanation.surface: A student finally set to take up biology.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means in a state of preparation, a synonym for prepared.

clue.text: Longing for 20 in Osaka?

definitions.meaning: 20 is READY, slang for cash; in Japan the money

explanation.surface: Desire for preparedness in a Japanese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready (short for ready money) is British slang for cash, and Osaka is in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Yen means a yearning, and the yen is Japan's currency, its ready money.

clue.text: Knowledge test for the upper classes

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: An exam to qualify for high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are people of good birth and social standing, the class below the nobility.

clue.text: Agitated Poles eating fish

indicators.note: eating means the poles take the fish inside them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Polish people getting worked up over a fish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but means the compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken means disturbed or upset, so agitated in feeling.
